findings.title: Reviewer rejection cannot restore tracked files
findings.why_it_matters: The reviewer-rejection path must reliably remove rejected source changes before audit artifacts are committed and the next loop begins.
findings.what_is_wrong: Step 3 records each tracked path as a blob SHA, then routes `git checkout <blob-sha> -- <path>`. Git checkout resolves that position as a tree-ish, so it exits 128 with `fatal: unable to read tree` and leaves the rejected change intact.
evidence: direct reproduction: git checkout <HEAD:path blob> -- tracked.txt exited 128 and retained changed content
findings.leverage_impact: One valid Git restore command fixes every tracked rejection path.
findings.locality_impact: The canonical Step-3 rejection route and its reviewer/evaluation mirrors repeat the same invalid command.
findings.metric_signal: Direct temporary-repository reproduction exits 128; no current selftest executes the restore command.
findings.why_weakens_submission: A rejected refactor can remain in the worktree, corrupting the promised commit-only-artifacts outcome and subsequent checkpoint state.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Replace the invalid blob checkout with `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <path>` in the canonical route and mirrors, retain null-path deletion, and add one temporary-repository selftest that proves a tracked staged+unstaged change returns to clean HEAD state.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: Rejected tracked changes must be restored before artifact-only commit.
simplification_check.helpful_simplification: Use Git restore from unchanged HEAD and exercise it once in a temporary repository.
simplification_check.should_not_be_done: Do not add a custom blob materializer or another checkpoint field.
simplification_check.tests_after_fix: Modify and stage a tracked file, run the documented restore, and assert clean status plus original content; then run the full suite.
